draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Ganpatipule! This little town of about 100 houses is home to a 400-year-old Ganpati idol that's said to have sprung up from the soil itself, and it faces west toward the sea.
draft.hungryLine: I don't have a named place to eat in Ganpatipule in my notes, so ask around near the temple.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Start at the Ganpati Temple right on the beach, then head 2 km to Malgund, the birthplace of the Marathi poet Keshavsut.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Try the Aare-Ware twin beaches or Malgund beach on either side of Ganpatipule beach.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Prachin Konkan is a life-size museum that recreates the old Konkan way of life, with houses, costumes and livelihoods.

spots.name: Ganpati Temple
spots.detail: On the beach · The swayambhu Ganpati that draws thousands of pilgrims

spots.name: Malgund
spots.detail: 2 km away · Poet Keshavsut's birthplace and memorial

spots.name: Jaigad fort
spots.detail: 15 km away · 17th-century ruins over the sea, and a lovely coastal drive

legends.title: Ganpati moves forward
legends.body: Local folklore says Ganpati took offence at something a local woman said and moved from his old home at Gule to Pule, meaning forward. That's how the place got the name Ganpati-pule.

legends.title: An idol from the earth
legends.body: The temple's idol is a swayambhu murti, said to have risen up out of the soil on its own about 400 years ago.

tips.title: Expect warm but not scorching days.
tips.body: After March it gets warmer here, though the temperature rarely crosses 30 °C.

tips.title: Make time for Prachin Konkan.
tips.body: This museum shows how people in old Konkan lived, worked and dressed.

story.title: From Gule to Pule
story.body: Folklore says Ganpati moved here from his original home at Gule, giving the town its name.

story.title: The swayambhu idol
story.body: The Ganpati idol here is said to have sprung up from the soil about four centuries ago.

story.title: Jaigad on guard
story.body: Jaigad fort was built in the 17th century, overlooking the point where the Sangameshwar river meets the Arabian Sea.

story.title: Pilgrims and beach lovers
story.body: Thousands of devotees from across Maharashtra visit every year, and the beaches nearby make it a holiday spot too.
